title: What Are Those Strange Noises Trump Makes?

In the run-up to last week’s midterm tsunami, I became perplexed by the way President Trump was talking. And because he is the same person now as he was then — and perhaps even “samer,” as he might say — I remain perplexed.


The issue is not that Trump often seems barely able to rub a noun and a verb together. I’ve generally felt that his barstool speaking style is partly a function of America’s increasingly informal approach to oratory, and partly because Trump realizes that his cult of personality eliminates the need to eloquently project authority.


And as I[wrote recently](https://www.nytimes.com/2026/10/08/opinion/trump-profanity.html) , his increasing use of profanity is due to the fact that novelty wears off and you have to always set the flame higher. Oreos now come not only in a Double Stuf variety — what a Dionysian blast that was for a kid when they were introduced in the 1970s — but now an even more padded Mega-Stuf. Mega-Stuf Trumpianese, including his recent forays into seemingly[homoerotic](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=gEfQSY9Ytts) asides, gets the audience going.


I’ve watched many Trump speeches over the years. But in his recent rallies, I saw something new.


Last month in South Carolina, Trump[referred](https://x.com/HQNewsNow/status/2113054759070392523?a=hIcpxwNW2hU-2vdt7XE&s=20) to the former South Carolina governor Nikki Haley as “the governor EEHHP.” It was a bizarre belch-like noise, something uncontrolled. Was Trump going for a dis of Haley? If so, it was an oddly clumsy one for a master of the stand-up put-down. “Governor EEHHP”?


The next day, discussing the Senate hopeful Abdul El-Sayed, Trump[said](https://x.com/atrupar/status/2113425022257639593) , “If you don’t want communists controlling the U.S. Senate which is between JAYYT … how about the gentleman from a place called Michigan?” The “JAYYT” has no meaning, and why “a place called Michigan,” as if Trump were referring to Brigadoon? Did it help him save face for a verbal glitch?


So: “EEHHP,” “JAYYT” — and then “jigger.” That one was in Mississippi, and it was Trump[referring](https://x.com/search?q=trump%20jigger&src=typed_query) to gas prices in Iowa being $1.85 “on the top of the jigger.” What’s a jigger? (A measuring tool for bartenders, sure — but what does that have to do with gas?)
